Inherited proximal tubulopathy with proteinuria and nephrocalcinosis; urinary calcium loss does not establish a separate systemic metabolic disorder.
Immune-mediated papillary inflammation of the conjunctiva associated with contact lenses.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with cerebellar hypoplasia.
Tuberculous infection of the ovary; reproductive location adds no organ axis.
Structural disorder confined to the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ.
Cerebellar ataxia; nystagmus reflects neurologic dysfunction. Hearing loss occurs in 3/17 and does not meet the threshold.
Muscular dystrophy with common peripheral nerve demyelination (>30%); asymptomatic white-matter changes alone would not qualify. Respiratory weakness is muscular.
Benign neoplasm arising in the anus.
Hypertension of the pulmonary vasculature; underlying lung disease is a separate cause, not direct pulmonary injury from this concept.
Cutaneous and visceral vascular tumors; liver involvement common, renal insufficiency/hypoplasia annotated 80-99%. Frequent cytopenias/coagulopathy omitted at the four-axis cap.
B-cell developmental failure with absent circulating B cells and antibodies. Recurrent ear and respiratory infections are separately diagnosed infections.
Cardiomyopathy and lentigines define the syndrome; structural chest/skeletal abnormalities occur in roughly half or more. Hearing loss is a minority feature.
Primary tuberculous infection of the digestive tract.
Inherited central movement disorder; additional organ disease varies across subtypes and is not shared by most patients.
GPI-anchor biosynthesis disorder with intellectual disability, seizures and ichthyosis; retinal coloboma 8/8. Hearing loss 8/8, cardiac and dental defects omitted at cap.
Hypothalamic endocrine dysfunction common (~50-70% in HPE); cleft palate and hearing loss each annotated 30-79%. Hypotelorism alone does not establish ocular injury.
Renal amyloidosis 4/4, hepatic amyloidosis 3/3; LYZ disease is usually non-neuropathic. Isolated sicca and heart failure do not establish common direct organ injury.
Mycobacterium ulcerans infection directly causes necrotizing skin ulcers.
Severe congenital encephalopathy with hypertonia and seizures. Respiratory failure reflects neurologic dysfunction without established direct lung injury.
Angiosarcoma arising in the ovary; the tumor's organ of origin is reproductive and has no axis.
Glycogen metabolism disorder predominantly affecting liver across the group; muscle disease is restricted to less common subtypes.
Bone fragility disorder; permanent tooth agenesis in 2/5 (40%). Motor delay alone does not establish neural injury; blue sclerae do not establish ocular damage.
Brittle sulfur-deficient hair defines the group; supplied neurologic, ocular and skeletal phenotypes are occasional (5-29%).
Excessive bone thickening; additional organ injury is not characteristic across the umbrella concept.
